purpose: Oxaprozin is used to relieve pain, swelling, and stiffness caused by arthritis, including rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis. It helps make it easier to move around and do everyday activities. Your doctor may also use it for other types of pain or inflammation.
how_it_works: Your body makes certain chemicals called prostaglandins that cause pain and swelling. Oxaprozin works by blocking the enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2) that your body uses to make these chemicals. With fewer of these chemicals around, you feel less pain and your joints are less swollen and stiff.
common_side_effects: Upset stomach, heartburn, nausea, diarrhea, constipation, dizziness, headache, and stomach pain are the most common side effects. Taking it with food or milk can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: This medicine can increase your risk of heart attack, stroke, and serious stomach or intestinal bleeding, especially with long-term use or at higher doses. Do not take it if you are allergic to aspirin or other NSAIDs. Avoid it if you have kidney problems, heart failure, or are in the last 3 months of pregnancy. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially blood thinners, because this medicine can interact with many drugs.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 600 mg to 1200 mg taken once a day, with or without food. Your doctor will choose the lowest dose that works for you. The maximum dose is 1800 mg per day (or 26 mg per kilogram of body weight, whichever is lower). Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
